mathlib_relation: Mathlib supplies weak-convergence tools. The permutation-array limit uses local exchangeable-transposition identities together with bundled StatLean permutation-marginal and Stein-method machinery.
notes: Exact double centering and variance normalization are premises; the maximum entry must vanish. This is an asymptotic theorem, without an optimal finite-sample distribution-function error bound.
statement:
Let $N_q\to\infty$ be natural row sizes, $\beta_q\to0$ a real sequence, and $c_q$ real $N_q\times N_q$ matrices. Eventually in $q$, assume $N_q\ge2$, every row and every column sums to zero, $\sum_{i,j}c_q(i,j)^2=N_q-1$, and $\lvert c_q(i,j)\rvert\le\beta_q$ for all $i,j$. Then for every bounded continuous real $f$,
$$
\frac1{N_q!}\sum_{\pi\in S_{N_q}}f\!\left(\sum_i c_q(i,\pi(i))\right)\longrightarrow\int f\,dN(0,1).
$$
Equivalently, under uniform permutations the permutation sums converge weakly to the standard normal law.
summary: Uniform permutation sums of doubly centered arrays have a standard normal limit when normalized entries vanish.
title: Combinatorial central limit theorem for permutation arrays
use: A common foundation for permutation tests, matching, and finite-population asymptotics, with no paper-specific objects in the signature.

mathlib_relation: Mathlib v4.34.1 CentralLimitTheorem.lean supplies the scalar iid CLT, including ProbabilityTheory.tendstoInDistribution_inv_sqrt_mul_sum_sub. This triangular-array extension allows changing row probability spaces and uses Mathlib independence, characteristic functions, Gaussian laws and Lévy convergence.
notes: Measurability, within-row joint independence, square integrability, centering, variance normalization and the Lindeberg condition are inputs. The triangular-array argument adapts StatLean/Stat-Lean. A bounded-array version in the same module, `lindeberg_clt_of_bounded`, supplies block-level normal limits in `P037_FiniteDesign.lean`.
statement:
For arbitrary finite row lengths $m_n$ and probability spaces $(\Omega_n,P_n)$, let measurable real $X_{ni}$, $i<m_n$, be jointly independent within each row, centered under $P_n$, and in $L^2(P_n)$. Assume $\sum_{i<m_n}\operatorname{Var}_{P_n}(X_{ni})\to1$ and, for every $\epsilon>0$,
$$
\sum_{i<m_n}\int_{\{\lvert X_{ni}\rvert>\epsilon\}}X_{ni}^2\,dP_n\longrightarrow0.
$$
Then $\sum_{i<m_n}X_{ni}$ converges in distribution to any random variable $Z$ with law $N(0,1)$ on any probability space $(\Omega',P')$. The formal conclusion uses Mathlib's weak convergence of laws.
summary: Independent centered triangular arrays converge to the standard normal law under variance normalization and the Lindeberg condition.
title: Lindeberg CLT on changing probability spaces
use: Supports independent clusters, triangular arrays, and conditional resampling arguments without forcing a common row space or identical distributions. No growth condition on $m_n$ or relationship between rows is assumed.

mathlib_relation: Mathlib v4.34.1 supplies Radon–Nikodym derivatives, weak convergence and Portmanteau tools. The local asymptotic-statistics interface combines these ingredients into event, statistic and subsequential likelihood-ratio characterizations of contiguity.
notes: The contiguity direction is vanishing under P implies vanishing under Q. Mutual absolute continuity is an explicit premise of this four-way theorem. Radon–Nikodym derivatives are converted from extended nonnegative values to real values.
statement:
Let $P_n,Q_n$ be probability measures on arbitrary measurable spaces $\Omega_n$, with $P_n\ll Q_n$ and $Q_n\ll P_n$ for every $n$. The following four statements are equivalent.

1. For every sequence of measurable $A_n\subseteq\Omega_n$, $P_n(A_n)\to0$ implies $Q_n(A_n)\to0$.
2. For every sequence of measurable real $T_n$, if $P_n(\lvert T_n\rvert\ge\epsilon)\to0$ for every $\epsilon>0$, then $Q_n(\lvert T_n\rvert\ge\epsilon)\to0$ for every $\epsilon>0$.
3. For every strictly increasing $\phi:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N$ and every probability measure $U$ on $\mathbb R$, if the $Q_{\phi(k)}$-laws of $(dP_{\phi(k)}/dQ_{\phi(k)}).\mathrm{toReal}$ converge weakly to $U$, then $U((0,\infty))=1$.
4. For every such $\phi$ and every probability measure $V$ on $\mathbb R$, if the $P_{\phi(k)}$-laws of $(dQ_{\phi(k)}/dP_{\phi(k)}).\mathrm{toReal}$ converge weakly to $V$, then $\int x\,dV(x)=1$.

Weak convergence means convergence of integrals of every bounded continuous real test function.
summary: Contiguity is equivalent to transfer of negligible statistics and two subsequential likelihood-ratio criteria under mutual absolute continuity.
title: Le Cam’s first lemma, four equivalent forms
use: Gives interchangeable event, statistic, and likelihood-ratio criteria for transferring negligible remainders between experiments. It applies to changing observation spaces and quantifies over all subsequential probability limits, without assuming convergence of the entire likelihood-ratio sequence.

mathlib_relation: Mathlib supplies Radon–Nikodym, Lp and probability machinery. The local StatLean-based QMD machinery adds square-root transport, likelihood and product-Hellinger controls for the nondominated expansion.
notes: This is a scalar, right-sided path at local scale inverse square root of sample size; no common global dominator is assumed. The likelihood uses the Radon–Nikodym derivative of the absolutely continuous part. Lean uses log zero equal to zero, and the expansion does not assert everywhere-positive likelihoods. No Gaussian score limit is asserted by this declaration alone.
statement:
Let $P$ be a probability on an arbitrary measurable space $\Omega$, let $P_t$ be a probability for every real $t\ge0$, and assume $P_0=P$. Let $g:\Omega\to\mathbb R$ be measurable. For $\nu_t=P+P_t$, assume
$$
\frac{\left\|\sqrt{(dP_t/d\nu_t).\mathrm{toReal}}-\sqrt{(dP/d\nu_t).\mathrm{toReal}}-\frac t2g\sqrt{(dP/d\nu_t).\mathrm{toReal}}\right\|_{L^2(\nu_t)}}{t}\longrightarrow0\qquad(t\downarrow0).
$$
The norm and quotient here take extended nonnegative values. For measurable iid $X_i$ of law $P$ on any probability space $(\Omega',P')$, the conclusions are $E_Pg=0$, integrability of $g^2$ under $P$, and
$$
\sum_{i<n}\log\!\left((dP_{1/\sqrt n}/dP)(X_i).\mathrm{toReal}\right)-\frac1{\sqrt n}\sum_{i<n}g(X_i)+\frac12\int g^2\,dP\longrightarrow0
$$
in $P'$-measure.
summary: One-sided quadratic-mean differentiability yields a centered square-integrable score and a local likelihood expansion without a common dominator.
title: One-sided nondominated QMD gives score regularity and a local likelihood expansion
use: Supplies a LAN expansion for changing support and singular perturbations, deriving the score moments instead of assuming them. The path is scalar and may have no common dominating measure.

mathlib_relation: Mathlib v4.34.1 supplies normed spaces, continuous linear maps, tightness and convergence tools. This theorem combines them with the local outer-expectation and sequential tangential derivative conventions and StatLean outer mapping and Slutsky tools.
notes: Scalar output, a tight limit, a closed separable tangent set, eventual domain membership for every sample point, and measurable scalar readouts are explicit premises. Neither the original paths nor their linear readouts are required to be measurable.
statement:
Let $E$ be a real normed space with its Borel measurable structure, $\mu$ a probability on a measurable space $\Omega$, $D,H\subseteq E$, $\theta\in D$, and $H$ closed and separable. Suppose $T:E\to\mathbb R$ and a continuous linear map $L:E\to\mathbb R$ satisfy the following sequential tangential derivative condition: for every $h\in H$, every $t_n>0$ with $t_n\to0$, and every $h_n\to h$ with $\theta+t_nh_n\in D$ for all $n$,
$$
\frac{T(\theta+t_nh_n)-T(\theta)}{t_n}\longrightarrow Lh.
$$
Let $r_n\to+\infty$ and let arbitrary maps $Z_n:\Omega\to E$ satisfy the uniform eventual domain condition: there exists $n_0\in\mathbb N$ such that $Z_n(\omega)\in D$ for every $n\ge n_0$ and every $\omega\in\Omega$. Suppose $r_n(Z_n-\theta)$ converges outer weakly to a tight probability $\nu$ with $\nu(H^c)=0$: for every bounded continuous real test function, both its upper and lower expectations converge to its $\nu$-integral. Upper expectation is the infimum of integrals of measurable integrable pointwise majorants; lower expectation is minus the upper expectation of the negative function. Assume also that each $T\circ Z_n$ is measurable. Put $R_n=r_n\{T(Z_n)-T(\theta)\}-L\{r_n(Z_n-\theta)\}$. Then $\mu^*(\lvert R_n\rvert\ge\epsilon)\to0$ for every $\epsilon>0$, and the CDF of $r_n\{T(Z_n)-T(\theta)\}$ converges to that of $\nu\circ L^{-1}$ at every continuity point. Here $\mu^*$ is the outer-measure value on an arbitrary event, so the remainder need not be measurable.
summary: Tangential Hadamard differentiability transfers outer weak convergence to a scalar limit and controls the actual linearization remainder.
title: Scalar outer Hadamard delta method
use: Useful for empirical processes and functional estimators with potentially nonmeasurable paths and arbitrary diverging rates. Here outer weak convergence requires both upper and lower expectations of every bounded continuous test to converge; $H$ need not be a linear subspace.

mathlib_relation: Mathlib v4.34.1 provides Measure.eq_of_cdf and covariance_eq_sub. This theorem adapts the bundled Causalean monotone/countermonotone product-loss optimality theorem to centered-coordinate covariance extrema. Its coupling and quantile foundations come from the Causalean library.
notes: Both marginals must have finite second moments. The covariance extrema follow from the monotone and countermonotone product-loss coupling theorem in the bundled Causalean library.

related_declarations.role: equivalence of CDF and marginal-law compatibility

statement:
Let $H$ be a Borel probability on $\mathbb R^2$ whose two coordinate functions are in $L^2(H)$, with marginal laws $\mu,\nu$ and lower generalized-inverse quantiles $Q_\mu,Q_\nu$, where $Q_\mu(u)=\inf\{x:u\le F_\mu(x)\}$. Write $X(x,y)=x$ and $Y(x,y)=y$. Let $\mathcal C(H)$ be all Borel probability laws with the same two marginal CDFs as $H$. Put
$$
c_+=\int_{(0,1)}Q_\mu(u)Q_\nu(u)\,du-E_HX\,E_HY,\qquad c_-=\int_{(0,1)}Q_\mu(u)Q_\nu(1-u)\,du-E_HX\,E_HY.
$$
Then $\sup_{J\in\mathcal C(H)}\operatorname{Cov}_J(X,Y)=c_+$ and $\inf_{J\in\mathcal C(H)}\operatorname{Cov}_J(X,Y)=c_-$. There exists a compatible law attaining $c_+$ and a compatible law attaining $c_-$. Covariance is the integral of the product of centered coordinates.
summary: Quantile couplings attain the largest and smallest covariances compatible with two square-integrable marginal laws.
title: Attained Fréchet covariance bounds for square-integrable marginals
use: Directly useful for sharp covariance and treatment-effect-variance identification, including atomic, mixed, and continuous distributions.

mathlib_relation: Mathlib’s scalar iid CLT supplies the limit theorem for the first projection. This result adds the order-two projection decomposition and a negligible degenerate remainder, using local dyad and product-measure interfaces.
notes: The kernel is scalar and the statistic averages all unordered pairs. Zero first-projection variance gives a degenerate Gaussian limit at this normalization; the theorem alone supplies neither studentization nor nondegenerate inference.
statement:
Let $\mu$ be a probability on any measurable space $U$, and let $h:U\times U\to\mathbb R$ be measurable, pointwise symmetric, in $L^2(\mu\otimes\mu)$, and centered under $\mu\otimes\mu$. Put $g(u)=\int h(u,v)\,d\mu(v)$ and $D_N=N(N-1)/2$. On the infinite iid product space with law $\mu^{\mathbb N}$ and coordinates $U_i$,
$$
\sqrt N\,D_N^{-1}\sum_{0\le i<j<N}h(U_i,U_j)\Rightarrow N\!\left(0,4\int g^2\,d\mu\right).
$$
The formal conclusion is Mathlib convergence in distribution to the identity random variable under this Gaussian law. The nonnegative variance is represented using toNNReal. Division at $N=0,1$ is totalized in Lean and does not affect the limit.
summary: Centered symmetric pairwise averages have a Gaussian limit under square integrability, including zero projection variance.
title: Order-two U-statistic CLT under only second moments
use: A general limit theorem for pairwise statistics, dyadic estimators and projection arguments; boundedness and a regression model are unnecessary.

group: Dependency-graph quadratic forms and spectral repair
mathlib_relation: Mathlib v4.34.1 has matrix spectral theory, Matrix.PosSemidef and CFC positive parts, including CFC.posPart_nonneg and positive/negative-part identities. This development supplies the explicit Frobenius projection inequality and companion nearest-matrix and uniqueness results for the spectral positive part.
notes: The input matrix is real and symmetric. The headline declaration is the projection inequality; the nearest-matrix and uniqueness statements use companion results. No least-majorant assertion in Loewner order is made.

related_declarations.role: PSD membership of the clipped matrix

statement:
For every natural $n$, every real symmetric $n\times n$ matrix $M$, and every real positive-semidefinite $n\times n$ matrix $X$, let $M_+$ replace each negative eigenvalue of $M$ by zero and let $\lVert A\rVert_F^2=\sum_{i,j}A_{ij}^2$. The declaration states
$$
\lVert M_+-M\rVert_F^2+\lVert X-M_+\rVert_F^2\le\lVert X-M\rVert_F^2.
$$
The nearest-matrix and uniqueness conclusions are exposed by companion declarations; PSD membership of $M_+$ comes from the surrounding positive-part API.
summary: Clipping negative eigenvalues gives a Frobenius projection inequality that yields the unique nearest positive-semidefinite matrix.
title: Nearest positive-semidefinite matrix in Frobenius norm
use: Useful for covariance repair, matrix optimization and numerical linear algebra, independently of a probability model or graph. The squared-distance remainder also quantifies the loss from a competing PSD matrix.

mathlib_relation: The pinned Mathlib supplies multivariateGaussian, its characteristic function and covariance identities in Probability/Distributions/Gaussian/Multivariate.lean, together with standard Gaussian measure and scalar moment-generating tools. This theorem gives equality of the exponentially tilted Gaussian measure and the Gaussian measure with shifted mean.
notes: Finite-dimensional real Gaussian laws and linear exponential tilts only; this is not an infinite-dimensional Cameron–Martin theorem. Covariance invertibility is not assumed.
statement:
For any finite coordinate type with decidable equality, every real positive-semidefinite covariance matrix $S$, and every vector $h$ in the corresponding Euclidean space,
$$
\exp\!\left(\langle h,y\rangle-\frac12h^TSh\right)N(0,S)(dy)=N(Sh,S)(dy)
$$
as an equality of measures. The left side is formally the centered Gaussian measure with nonnegative density $\operatorname{ofReal}(\exp(\langle h,y\rangle-h^TSh/2))$. The mean on the right is multiplication by $S$ viewed as a continuous linear map.
summary: A normalized linear exponential tilt shifts a finite-dimensional Gaussian mean by its covariance times the tilt vector.
title: Exponential tilting of possibly singular Gaussian laws
use: A short measure-level change-of-law interface for Gaussian shifts, local alternatives and Le Cam calculations. Singular $S$, including $S=0$, is allowed.

mathlib_relation: Mathlib supplies Radon–Nikodym derivatives, product integration and Lp inequalities. The local Hellinger product bound factors affinity over coordinates and applies a power inequality.
notes: The convention is the unscaled square-root density difference. Both measures are probabilities, domination is common and sigma-finite, and the products have identical independent factors; arbitrary dependent laws are outside this statement.
statement:
Let probability measures $\mu,\nu$ on any measurable space $\Omega$ be absolutely continuous with respect to a common $\sigma$-finite measure $\xi$. Put $p=(d\mu/d\xi).\mathrm{toReal}$ and $q=(d\nu/d\xi).\mathrm{toReal}$. For every natural $n$,
$$
\left\|\sqrt{\prod_{j<n}p(x_j)}-\sqrt{\prod_{j<n}q(x_j)}\right\|_{L^2(\xi^{\otimes n})}\le\sqrt n\,\left\|\sqrt p-\sqrt q\right\|_{L^2(\xi)}.
$$
The formal signature takes square roots of the real values of products of extended Radon–Nikodym derivatives and compares the real values of the extended $L^2$ norms. Companion integrability lemmas establish finiteness of the residual norms.
summary: The square-root density error for independent repeated observations grows at most with the square root of sample size.
title: Hellinger error tensorization for product experiments
use: Converts one-observation approximation into an experiment-level bound for testing, LAN and asymptotic equivalence on arbitrary observation spaces.

mathlib_relation: The pinned Mathlib supplies a scalar iid CLT, multivariate Gaussian measures and Lévy characteristic-function convergence. This theorem combines those tools through a local bounded-continuous-test weak-convergence interface.
notes: Finite-dimensional iid observations and a finite second moment are required. The covariance matrix may be singular. This is separate from the changing-space, nonidentically distributed Lindeberg array theorem.
statement:
For any natural $k$, let measurable iid $Y_i:\Omega\to\mathbb R^k$ on a probability space with law $P$ satisfy $Y_0\in L^2(P)$ and $E_P\langle u,Y_0\rangle=0$ for every $u$. Let $\Sigma$ be a specified real positive-semidefinite matrix and assume, for every $u,v\in\mathbb R^k$,
$$
E_P[\langle u,Y_0\rangle\langle v,Y_0\rangle]=u^T\Sigma v.
$$
Then the laws of $n^{-1/2}\sum_{i<n}Y_i$ converge weakly to $N(0,\Sigma)$: the integrals of every bounded continuous real test function converge to its Gaussian integral.
summary: Sums of centered iid vectors with finite second moments converge after square-root normalization to a Gaussian law with the specified covariance, which may be singular.
title: Multivariate iid CLT allowing singular covariance
use: A direct entry point for vector scores, estimators and joint limits in any finite dimension, without covariance invertibility.

mathlib_relation: Mathlib v4.34.1 supplies finite sums, ordered-field inequalities and intermediate-value tools used here. The threshold optimizers and attainable-interval result use local ratio and feasible-box definitions.
notes: Sorting and strictly positive masses are required; ties and $\alpha=\beta$ are allowed. Cuts are zero-based prefix lengths. Sharpness concerns the box of real weights; integer population-size or known-size compatibility constraints are not imposed.

related_declarations.role: set of ratios over the real weight box

statement:
Let $n>0$, let $y_0\le\cdots\le y_{n-1}$ be real outcomes, let $a_i>0$ be real masses, and assume $0<\alpha\le\beta\le1$. Put $\gamma=\beta/\alpha$ and $R(w)=\sum_i a_iw_iy_i/\sum_i a_iw_i$. For $0\le k<n$, define $u^L_{k,i}=\gamma$ for $i<k$ and $1$ otherwise, and $u^H_{k,i}=1$ for $i<k$ and $\gamma$ otherwise; write $L_k=R(u^L_k)$ and $H_k=R(u^H_k)$.

There exist least cuts $k_L,k_H\in\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$ satisfying $L_{k_L}\le y_{k_L}$ and $H_{k_H}\le y_{k_H}$, respectively. The weights $w^L=u^L_{k_L}/\beta$ and $w^H=u^H_{k_H}/\beta$ belong to $[1/\beta,1/\alpha]^n$ and have ratios $L_{k_L}$ and $H_{k_H}$. These ratios are, respectively, the least and greatest elements of the attainable set $\{R(w):w\in[1/\beta,1/\alpha]^n\}$. They equal its real infimum and supremum, and the entire attainable set is exactly $[L_{k_L},H_{k_H}]$.
summary: Threshold weights attain the extreme bounded-weight means, and feasible weights attain every value between them.
title: Sharp bounded-weight means with explicit threshold optimizers
use: Gives explicit endpoint optimizers and the full interval for sensitivity analysis with bounded inverse-selection weights and arbitrary positive base masses. Unit masses and positive outcome-class masses are both covered.

mathlib_relation: Mathlib supplies conditional expectation and independence infrastructure. The causal IPW and double-robust identification identities use the local IsCEF and CI definitions.
notes: Uniform overlap and integrable potential outcomes are assumed. These are population equalities, without a consistency or efficiency conclusion for estimated nuisance functions. The true-propensity branch does not require correct outcome regressions or a separate overlap assumption on q.
statement:
On any probability space with law $\mu$, let $K$ be a natural number, $X:\Omega\to\mathbb R^K$ measurable, and $Y_0,Y_1,D$ measurable real variables. Assume $Y_0,Y_1\in L^1(\mu)$, $D\in\{0,1\}$ almost surely, and $P(D=0),P(D=1)>0$. Let $p$ be a conditional expectation function of $D$ given $X$ in the source's `IsCEF` sense, and assume that some $\epsilon>0$ satisfies $\epsilon<p(X)<1-\epsilon$ almost surely. Assume $(Y_0,Y_1)\perp D\mid X$ in the source's `CI` sense. Here `IsCEF` requires measurability of the function, integrability of the variable and fitted conditional mean, and equality of their integrals over every measurable covariate event; `CI` requires conditional-expectation factorization for every pair of measurable events.

Put $Y=DY_1+(1-D)Y_0$. Then
$$
E(Y_1-Y_0)=E\left[\frac{DY}{p(X)}-\frac{(1-D)Y}{1-p(X)}\right].
$$
Moreover, for every measurable $m_0,m_1,q:\mathbb R^K\to\mathbb R$ with $m_0(X),m_1(X)\in L^1(\mu)$,
$$
E(Y_1-Y_0)=E\left[m_1(X)+\frac{D(Y-m_1(X))}{q(X)}-m_0(X)-\frac{(1-D)(Y-m_0(X))}{1-q(X)}\right]
$$
provided either (a) $m_a$ is an `IsCEF` of $Y$ given $X$ under the unnormalized restricted measure $\mu\vert_{\{D=a\}}$ for each $a\in\{0,1\}$, and some $\eta>0$ satisfies $\eta<q(X)<1-\eta$ almost surely, or (b) $q(X)=p(X)$ almost surely.
summary: Identifies the average treatment effect by inverse weighting and gives the two alternatives for double robustness.
title: Causal IPW and double-robust identification
use: Provides population identification identities for causal IPW and augmented IPW, with the precise outcome-regression and propensity alternatives behind double robustness. The probability space is arbitrary; covariates have finitely many real coordinates.

mathlib_relation: Mathlib v4.34.1 supplies pushforwards, withDensity, measure extensionality and conditional expectation. The statistical addition is the MAR event reweighting identity and its extension to equality of outcome laws through the CEF/CI interface.
notes: Binary response and the strict positive lower bound are pointwise assumptions in this declaration. The result concerns the specified population response function and supplies no fitted-model guarantee.
statement:
Let $\mu$ be a probability measure on any measurable space, let $X$ be measurable into any measurable type, and let $Y,R$ be measurable real variables. Assume $R(\omega)\in\{0,1\}$ for every $\omega$. Let $p$ be an `IsCEF` of $R$ given $X$: $p$ is measurable, $R$ and $p(X)$ are integrable, and their integrals agree over every measurable covariate event. For a real $\epsilon>0$, assume $p(X(\omega))>\epsilon$ for every $\omega$. Assume $Y\perp R\mid X$ in the `CI` sense of conditional-expectation factorization for every pair of measurable events.

Define $
u$ by the nonnegative extended-real density $d
u/d\mu=\operatorname{ofReal}(R/p(X))$. Then the pushforward outcome laws are equal: $Y_\#
u=Y_\#\mu$.
summary: Shows that inverse-response weighting recovers the entire outcome distribution under missingness at random.
title: MAR reweighting identifies the entire outcome law
use: Identifies probabilities of all outcome events at once, providing a foundation for missing-data distributions, quantiles and bounded outcome functionals. No outcome moment assumption is required, and the covariate space need not be finite dimensional.

group: Finite randomization, inclusion probabilities and variance
mathlib_relation: The development uses finite uniform-subset expectations, inclusion moments, an exact symmetric variance calculation and symmetrization to bound principal matrix sums under fixed-size sampling.
notes: Both zero row sums and zero column sums are required. The companion expectation formula and this bound assemble the full Lei–Ding quadratic sampling proposition without taking that published proposition as a hypothesis.

related_declarations.role: same bound in explicit finite-sum notation

statement:
Let $n,s$ be natural numbers with $n\ge4$ and $s\le n$, and let $S$ be uniform over all $s$-element subsets of $\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$. For any real $n\times n$ matrix $Q$ satisfying $\sum_jQ_{ij}=0$ for every row $i$ and $\sum_iQ_{ij}=0$ for every column $j$, put $X_Q(S)=\sum_{i\in S}\sum_{j\in S}Q_{ij}$. With variance defined as the uniform average of squared deviations over those subsets,
$$
\operatorname{Var}(X_Q)\le\frac{s(n-s)}{n(n-1)}\sum_i\sum_jQ_{ij}^2.
$$
summary: Bounds the variance of a principal matrix sum under sampling without replacement when every row and column sums to zero.
title: Quadratic-form sampling bound for doubly centered matrices
use: A reusable finite-sample variance bound for sampled matrix statistics and regression adjustment in completely randomized experiments. It allows nonsymmetric matrices and includes the empty and full samples; no positive-semidefiniteness, rank or trace restriction is imposed.

group: Finite randomization, inclusion probabilities and variance
mathlib_relation: Mathlib supplies general covariance, variance and finite-sum tools. The finite-design, exposure-probability and zero-joint-corrected estimator interfaces are defined here.
notes: Conservativeness is in design expectation. It is not a samplewise variance bound or a coverage guarantee. The exposure mapping and fixed potential outcomes are supplied as the finite Population object.
statement:
Let a finite assignment support have strictly positive real design masses summing to one. Let $N,K$ be natural numbers, let each unit's exposure be an arbitrary function of the assignment into $K$ exposure labels, and let $y_i(t)$ be fixed real potential outcomes. Choose distinct labels $d,e$ with $0<\pi_i(d)<1$ and $0<\pi_i(e)<1$ for every unit, where $\pi_i(t)=P(D_i=t)$. Then
$$
\operatorname{Var}(\widehat\tau_{HT})\le E[\widehat V],\qquad
\widehat\tau_{HT}=\frac1N\sum_i\left[\frac{I_i(d)y_i(d)}{\pi_i(d)}-\frac{I_i(e)y_i(e)}{\pi_i(e)}\right],
$$
where $\widehat V$ is the source's `effectVariance` estimator. Explicitly, when $N>0$, index exposure cells by $a=(i,t)$, $t\in\{d,e\}$, set $x_{i,d}=y_i(d)/N$, $x_{i,e}=-y_i(e)/N$, $I_a=\mathbf1\{D_i=t\}$, $\pi_a=E I_a$, and $\pi_{ab}=E(I_aI_b)$. Then
$$
\widehat V=\sum_{a,b:\pi_{ab}>0}I_aI_b\frac{\pi_{ab}-\pi_a\pi_b}{\pi_{ab}}\frac{x_a}{\pi_a}\frac{x_b}{\pi_b}
+\sum_{a,b:\pi_{ab}=0}\left(\frac{I_ax_a^2}{2\pi_a}+\frac{I_bx_b^2}{2\pi_b}\right).
$$
Both sums run over ordered cell pairs. In the source this is the two same-exposure HT variance estimators plus their zero-joint Young corrections, minus twice the corrected cross-exposure covariance, all divided by $N^2$. The Lean declaration also allows $N=0$; empty sums and totalized real division make both sides zero.
summary: Bounds the design variance of an exposure contrast by the expectation of a zero-joint-corrected variance estimator.
title: Conservative HT contrast variance with zero joint exposure probabilities
use: Handles finite interference designs with impossible joint exposures, where a usual unbiased pairwise variance estimator is unavailable. Potential outcomes may have either sign, and no positive-joint-probability assumption is required.

group: Finite randomization, inclusion probabilities and variance
mathlib_relation: Mathlib v4.34.1 supplies matrix and variance algebra. This theorem uses explicit OLS, leverage and complete-randomization definitions to express the HC2–Neyman identity and the expected variance gap.
notes: This is an unadjusted binary-treatment regression result under complete randomization, with at least two units in each arm. It concerns expected estimated variance, not expected standard error, and makes no claim for covariate-adjusted specifications.
statement:
Let the units be any finite type of size $N=n_1+n_0$, where $n_1,n_0\ge2$, with arbitrary fixed real potential outcomes $Y_i(1),Y_i(0)$. Randomize uniformly over all $n_1$-element treatment subsets. Let $\widehat\tau$ be the observed difference in means, let $V=\operatorname{Var}(\widehat\tau)$ under this design, and let $E$ be the design expectation of the HC2 sandwich slope variance from OLS with intercept and treatment indicator. The source defines HC2 from the inverse Gram matrix, OLS residuals and leverages, using $e_i^2/(1-h_i)$ in the sandwich.

Put $\tau_i=Y_i(1)-Y_i(0)$, $\bar\tau=N^{-1}\sum_i\tau_i$, and $S_\tau^2=(N-1)^{-1}\sum_i(\tau_i-\bar\tau)^2$. Then $E-V=S_\tau^2/N$, $V\le E$, and $E=V$ if and only if there exists $c\in\mathbb R$ with $\tau_i=c$ for every unit.
summary: Gives the exact expected HC2 variance gap and characterizes equality by constant treatment effects.
title: Exact HC2 conservativeness gap and equality condition
use: Connects the actual HC2 matrix calculation to the finite-population treatment-effect heterogeneity gap. The companion identity equating HC2 to the Neyman estimate provides a useful check for an unadjusted regression implementation.

group: Finite randomization, inclusion probabilities and variance
mathlib_relation: Mathlib v4.34.1 provides covariance_eq_sub and covariance linearity lemmas in Probability/Moments/Covariance.lean. This module uses its own finite weighted expectation and covariance to state the fitted-prediction design-bias identity.
notes: The same prediction is used in both arms, so the augmentation terms cancel in the displayed contrast. N need not equal the number of indices. Independence from individual fitting inputs alone does not imply independence from their fitted joint function.
statement:
Let $\Omega,I$ be finite types and let $R$ be any linearly ordered field. Let a finite design have nonnegative weights summing to one and binary assignments $T_i:\Omega\to\{0,1\}$. Assume $\pi_{1i}=ET_i>0$ and $\pi_{0i}=E(1-T_i)>0$ for every $i$. For arbitrary fixed $y_1,y_0:I\to R$, arbitrary assignment-dependent predictions $f:\Omega\times I\to R$, and any positive natural normalization $N$, define
$$
\widehat\Delta_G=\frac1N\sum_i\left[\frac{T_i(y_{1i}-f_i)}{\pi_{1i}}-\frac{(1-T_i)(y_{0i}-f_i)}{\pi_{0i}}\right],\qquad
\Delta=\frac1N\sum_i(y_{1i}-y_{0i}).
$$
Expectation is the weighted finite design sum and $\operatorname{Cov}(U,V)=E(UV)-EU\,EV$. Then
$$
E\widehat\Delta_G-\Delta=-\frac1N\sum_i\operatorname{Cov}(T_i,f_i)\left(\frac1{\pi_{1i}}+\frac1{\pi_{0i}}\right).
$$
summary: Expresses regression-assisted contrast bias exactly through covariances of treatment indicators and fitted predictions.
title: Exact prediction-covariance bias of regression-assisted contrasts
use: Expresses prediction-induced bias as a weighted sum of design covariances. Zero assignment–prediction covariance at every index is sufficient for unbiasedness. It allows arbitrary finite designs and assignment-dependent fitting, with no independence assumption. The normalization can represent original units even when the index set represents cluster totals.

mathlib_relation: Mathlib supplies measure pushforwards and integrals. The sharp ATE completion uses local observed-outcome and event-mean definitions.
notes: Bounded potential outcomes and positive probabilities of both observed arms are required. The result does not impose covariate-specific or additional cross-world restrictions. The alternative outcomes use the original space and treatment variable.

related_declarations.role: arm mean as a normalized event integral

statement:
On any probability space let $Y_0,Y_1,D$ be measurable real variables. For real $a,b$, assume $Y_0,Y_1\in[a,b]$ almost surely, $D\in\{0,1\}$ almost surely, and $\pi_j=P(D=j)>0$ for both $j=0,1$. Put $Y=DY_1+(1-D)Y_0$ and $m_j=\pi_j^{-1}\int_{\{D=j\}}Y\,d\mu$. Define
$$
L=\pi_1m_1+a\pi_0-(\pi_0m_0+b\pi_1),\qquad
U=\pi_1m_1+b\pi_0-(\pi_0m_0+a\pi_1).
$$
Then $E(Y_1-Y_0)\in[L,U]$ and $U-L=b-a$. For every real $c\in[L,U]$, there exist measurable $Z_0,Z_1$ on the same probability space, both in $[a,b]$ almost surely, such that the law of $(DZ_1+(1-D)Z_0,D)$ equals the law of $(Y,D)$ and $E(Z_1-Z_0)=c$.
summary: Constructs every bounded-outcome average treatment effect compatible with the same observed outcome and treatment law.
title: Sharp ATE interval with unchanged observable law
use: Gives both valid bounds and attainment of every value through observationally equivalent counterfactual completions, without ignorability. The interval width is exactly the outcome-support width, regardless of treatment imbalance.

mathlib_relation: Mathlib v4.34.1 provides probability measures, finite counting and floor arithmetic. This theorem combines those tools with coordinate-permutation invariance to establish corrected p-value validity and the one-sided floor bounds.
notes: The observed coordinate is included through the explicit plus-one correction, and both rank comparisons are weak. Exchangeability must hold for the actual simulation protocol; correct marginal laws alone do not establish it. Ties can make the bounds conservative.
statement:
Let $B>0$ be a natural number. Let $(T_0,\ldots,T_B)$ have any probability law on $\mathbb R^{B+1}$ invariant under every coordinate permutation. Define
$$
L=\frac{1+\#\{b=1,\ldots,B:T_b\le T_0\}}{B+1},\qquad
U=\frac{1+\#\{b=1,\ldots,B:T_0\le T_b\}}{B+1},\qquad
p_2=\min(1,2\min(L,U)).
$$
For every real $\alpha\in[0,1]$,
$$
P(L\le\alpha)\le\frac{\lfloor\alpha(B+1)\rfloor}{B+1},\qquad
P(U\le\alpha)\le\frac{\lfloor\alpha(B+1)\rfloor}{B+1},\qquad
\frac{\lfloor\alpha(B+1)\rfloor}{B+1}\le\alpha,\qquad
P(p_2\le\alpha)\le\alpha.
$$
summary: Establishes finite-sample validity of corrected exchangeable Monte Carlo tails and their doubled minimum.
title: Exchangeable Monte Carlo p-values, with ties and floor bounds
use: Provides finite-sample validity for simulation and permutation tests whenever the entire observed-and-reference statistic vector is exchangeable. The reference statistics may be dependent and may tie.

group: Dependency-graph quadratic forms and spectral repair
mathlib_relation: Mathlib v4.34.1 supplies covariance and variance expansions and Euclidean operator norms. The DepGraph interface used here is vendored Causalean code in this repository. The local theorem gives an explicit variance bound for dense quadratic forms under that dependency-graph interface.
notes: Centered bounded coordinates, a deterministic symmetric matrix and full tuple independence off the graph are required. Pairwise zero covariance is insufficient. The degree bound includes self; the declaration itself is a variance inequality, not an asymptotic consistency theorem.
statement:
On any probability space with law $\mu$, let $n$ be a natural number and let $Z_i$, $i\in\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$, be measurable real variables with $EZ_i=0$. Let $B\ge0$ satisfy $|Z_i|\le B$ almost surely for every $i$. Suppose a reflexive symmetric relation $G$ is a dependency graph in the source's `DepGraph` sense: for any two finite index sets with no connecting edge, their variable tuples are independent. Let a real $d\ge0$ satisfy $\sum_j\mathbf1\{G(i,j)\}\le d$ for every row $i$, counting the self-edge.

For every deterministic symmetric real matrix $A$,
$$
\operatorname{Var}\left(\sum_i\sum_j A_{ij}Z_iZ_j\right)\le(144d^3+2d^2)B^4\lVert A\rVert_{op}^2n,
$$
where $\lVert A\rVert_{op}$ is the Euclidean operator norm. The dependency-graph structure bundles measurability and the stated tuple-independence property.
summary: Bounds the variance of dense quadratic forms of centered bounded variables with a dependency graph.
title: Dense quadratic variance bound under a genuine dependency graph
use: Gives an explicit finite-sample variance bound that can support consistency arguments for dense quadratic variance estimators in network or spatial models. The matrix need not be sparse, and the constant is explicit without an optimality claim.

mathlib_relation: Mathlib supplies convex-integral and Jensen tools in Analysis/Convex/Integral and integral-positivity criteria in MeasureTheory/Integral/Bochner/Basic. The exact representability characterization and its weight constructions are defined here.
notes: The characterization uses an ordinary finite ratio. Weights may depend on the entire underlying state. They need not be bounded or positive everywhere, and the existence statement does not supply estimability from observed covariates.

related_declarations.role: construction when the target has positive mass
construction from positive mass on both sides

statement:
Let $G$ be any probability measure on a measurable space, let $\tau$ be a measurable integrable real function, and let $t\in\mathbb R$. There exists a measurable weight $w$ that is nonnegative at every point, satisfies $w,w\tau\in L^1(G)$ and $E_Gw>0$, and has $E_G(w\tau)/E_Gw=t$, if and only if
$$
P_G(\tau=t)>0\quad\text{or}\quad\bigl(P_G(\tau<t)>0\ \text{and}\ P_G(\tau>t)>0\bigr).
$$
summary: Characterizes attainable nonnegative weighted means by an atom at the target or positive probability on both sides.
title: Exactly which means nonnegative reweighting can represent
use: Adds an exact converse to weighted-average support restrictions. It describes representable weighted causal effects and transport or selection targets, including the positive-atom requirement for attainable support extremes.

group: Finite randomization, inclusion probabilities and variance
mathlib_relation: Mathlib v4.34.1 supplies Lebesgue interval measures, finite sums and indicator integrals. The systematic-sampling construction combines them with cumulative intervals and a fixed-spacing selection rule.
notes: The unit ordering and half-open intervals are part of the construction. Zero target probabilities are outside this interface. It fixes sample size and first-order marginals, without prescribing second-order inclusion probabilities.
statement:
Let $N\ge2$ and $m$ be natural numbers with $0<m<N$. Let real numbers $\pi_k$, $0\le k<N$, satisfy $0<\pi_k\le1$ for every $k$ and $\sum_k\pi_k=m$. Put $L_k=\sum_{a<k}\pi_a$ and select $k$ at start $u$ precisely when $L_k\le u+j<L_k+\pi_k$ for some integer $0\le j<m$. The spacing in `systematicSelected` is $\sum_k\pi_k/m=1$. For every real $u$ with $0\le u<1$, the set of selected units has cardinality exactly $m$. Moreover, for every $k$,

$$
\int_{[0,1)}\mathbf1\{k\text{ is selected at }u\}\,du=\pi_k.
$$
summary: Systematic sampling realizes any strictly positive admissible inclusion vector with an exactly fixed sample size.
title: Fixed-size systematic sampling with prescribed inclusion probabilities
use: Constructs an unequal-probability design for every strictly positive first-order inclusion vector satisfying the fixed-size feasibility constraints. The proof combines the cumulative-interval selection rule with exact cardinality and marginal-integral lemmas; it requires no outcome or superpopulation model.

mathlib_relation: Mathlib v4.34.1 provides Bernoulli and product laws, conditional expectations and limit machinery. This declaration gives uniform-estimation and honest-interval impossibility results for observed-data procedures with an arbitrary independent seed.
notes: This is a binary-outcome subclass with unrestricted measurable nuisance functions. The conclusions concern worst-case estimation and interval width at one fixed baseline, without asserting pointwise estimation failure at every law. Endpoints may be infinite and need not be ordered.

related_declarations.role: Width event under the fixed baseline

statement:
Let $\mathcal L$ consist of complete-unit probability laws $L$ for $(W,A,Y(0),Y(1))$ with $W$ uniform on $(0,1]$, binary treatment and almost-surely binary potential outcomes, joint conditional ignorability given $W$, and a measurable propensity $e(W)\in[1/4,3/4]$ almost surely. Ignorability is encoded by conditional-expectation factorization for every measurable integrable test of the potential-outcome pair. Write $\tau_L=E_L[Y(1)-Y(0)]$. For any measurable seed space $R$ and probability law $Q$ on it, let $\mathbb P_{L,Q}=L^{\otimes\mathbb N}\otimes Q$. The seed is independent of the iid complete-unit sample; procedures see only the first $n$ observed records $(W,A,Y)$ and the seed, and use the same functions under every law.

For every sequence of measurable real estimators $E_n$ on those inputs and every $n\ge1$,

$$
\sup_{L\in\mathcal L}\mathbb P_{L,Q}(|E_n-\tau_L|\ge1/12)\ge1/2.
$$

There also exists $\eta>0$ such that $\limsup_{n\to\infty}\sup_{L\in\mathcal L}\mathbb P_{L,Q}(|E_n-\tau_L|>\eta)>0$.

For every pair of measurable extended-real endpoint sequences $\ell_n,h_n$ on those inputs and every $0<\alpha<1/2$, if

$$
\liminf_{n\to\infty}\inf_{L\in\mathcal L}\mathbb P_{L,Q}(\ell_n\le\tau_L\le h_n)\ge1-\alpha,
$$

then $\liminf_{n\to\infty}\mathbb P_{S,Q}(\ell_n+1/6<h_n)\ge1-2\alpha>0$. Here $S$ is the single fixed baseline law with independent uniform $W$, fair binary $A$ and fair binary $Y(1)$, and $Y(0)=0$. The width event uses extended-real addition and ordering.
summary: With unrestricted measurable propensity and outcome-regression classes, no procedure, even a randomized one, estimates the average treatment effect uniformly or gives uniformly honest intervals that shrink.
title: Unknown-propensity impossibility for arbitrary randomized procedures
use: Distinguishes causal identification and overlap from uniform estimability and honest shrinking inference. It covers all measurable procedures using observed data and an independent seed of any probability law, including deterministic procedures. The proof uses a two-family construction, agreement of observed laws on samples without cell collisions, and testing inequalities.

mathlib_relation: Mathlib supplies finite-set intersections, finite sums and matrix algebra. The dyadic sandwich decomposition follows from a local coefficient identity for each ordered record pair.
notes: Each member-specific clustering puts incident records together and treats each outsider record as a singleton. Bread factors and any common scaling must be absorbed consistently into the scores. The identity includes no small-sample multipliers, positive-semidefinite clipping or stochastic conservativeness conclusion.

related_declarations.role: Discrepancy from substituting an identifier-clustered component

statement:
Let the record, member and parameter types $R,M,P$ be finite, with decidable equality. Every record $r$ carries a dyad $d_r$, an unordered set of exactly two distinct members, and arbitrary real scores $z_r\in\mathbb R^P$. For a real record-pair pattern $A$, put $\mathcal S(A)=\sum_{r,s\in R}A_{rs}z_rz_s^T$, with ordered pair sums. Define $D_{rs}=\mathbf1\{d_r\cap d_s\ne\varnothing\}$, $Q_{rs}=\mathbf1\{d_r=d_s\}$, $I_{rs}=\mathbf1\{r=s\}$, and

$$
C_{i,rs}=\mathbf1\{i\in d_r\cap d_s\}+\mathbf1\{r=s,\ i\notin d_r\}\qquad(i\in M).
$$

Then the matrix identity is

$$
\sum_{i\in M}\mathcal S(C_i)-\mathcal S(Q)-(|M|-2)\mathcal S(I)=\mathcal S(D).
$$

Here $|M|-2$ is subtraction in the real numbers.
summary: A finite-sum identity decomposes the dyadic sandwich exactly when dyads may repeat.
title: Exact dyadic sandwich decomposition with repeated dyads
use: Gives an implementation-ready exact identity for dyadic-cluster covariance calculations with repeated dyads and arbitrary finite labels. It is purely algebraic and permits arbitrary common scores. The proof reduces the matrix equality to a coefficient count for each ordered record pair.

mathlib_relation: Mathlib v4.34.1 supplies Gaussian laws, integration and finite probability infrastructure. This development combines permutation-array moment bounds with the bundled StatLean exchangeable-pair and Stein-equation machinery to obtain the explicit bounded-Lipschitz error estimate.
notes: This controls bounded Lipschitz tests rather than distribution-function distance. The assumptions include exact double centering, energy normalization and a global bound on the test function.
statement:
Let $N\ge3$ be natural and let $c$ be a real $N\times N$ matrix with every row and column sum zero and $\sum_{i,j}c(i,j)^2=N-1$. Let real $\beta$ satisfy $|c(i,j)|\le\beta$ for every $i,j$. Let $h:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ and real constants $L,C$ satisfy $L\ge0$, $|h(x)-h(y)|\le L|x-y|$ for every $x,y$, and $|h(x)|\le C$ for every $x$. For a uniform random permutation $\pi$ and $S=\sum_i c(i,\pi(i))$,

$$
\left|E_\pi h(S)-\int h\,dN(0,1)\right|\le32L\sqrt{\beta^2+1/N}+10L\beta.
$$

The expectation on the left is the arithmetic average over all permutations.
summary: A finite-sample bound controls Gaussian approximation for bounded Lipschitz functions of permutation sums.
title: Finite-sample bounded-Lipschitz bound for permutation arrays
use: Gives an explicit finite-sample approximation guarantee for globally bounded Lipschitz readouts of a normalized permutation statistic. It also supplies the quantitative step for the max-entry permutation CLT. The proof combines local exchangeable-transposition moment bounds with bundled StatLean Stein-equation estimates.

mathlib_relation: Mathlib v4.34.1 provides densities, product measures, Gaussian laws and weak-convergence ingredients. The density adapter connects these ingredients to the bundled StatLean QMD and local-experiment infrastructure.
notes: Scalar path and readout, at the specific local scale one over the square root of sample size. The QMD hypothesis is two-sided near zero and assumes both score centering and square integrability. The conclusion states contiguity of the alternative products with respect to the baseline products. The adapter depends on the bundled StatLean QMD and local-experiment infrastructure.
statement:
Let $E$ be an arbitrary measurable space and $\rho$ an S-finite measure. For every real $t$, let $p_t:E\to\mathbb R$ be measurable, pointwise nonnegative, and normalized by $\int p_t\,d\rho=1$ (the signature uses the nonnegative extended integral). Write $P_t=p_t\rho$ and $P=P_0$. Let $s,u:E\to\mathbb R$ be measurable, in $L^2(P)$, and both centered under $P$. Assume that for every $\varepsilon>0$ there is $\delta>0$ such that, for every real $t$ with $|t|<\delta$,
$$
\int\left(\sqrt{p_t}-\sqrt{p_0}-\frac{t}{2}s\sqrt{p_0}\right)^2d\rho\le\varepsilon t^2.
$$
Set $Q_n=P_{1/\sqrt n}$. Then $Q_n^{\otimes n}$ is contiguous with respect to $P^{\otimes n}$: for every sequence of measurable events $A_n$, $P^{\otimes n}(A_n)\to0$ implies $Q_n^{\otimes n}(A_n)\to0$. Under $Q_n^{\otimes n}$,
$$
n^{-1/2}\sum_{i<n}u(X_i)\ \Rightarrow\ N\!\left(E_P[us],E_P[u^2]\right).
$$
Here convergence means that, for every bounded continuous $f:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$, the expectation of $f(n^{-1/2}\sum_{i<n}u(X_i))$ under $Q_n^{\otimes n}$ converges to $\int f\,dN(E_P[us],E_P[u^2])$.
summary: Quadratic mean differentiability gives local product contiguity and a shifted Gaussian limit for centered readouts.
title: Density QMD score shift and contiguity
use: Provides a density-based entry point for local asymptotic experiments and influence-function limits. The readout can be any centered square-integrable real function; changing support and zero limiting variance are allowed. The adapter uses the bundled StatLean QMD and local-experiment infrastructure.

mathlib_relation: Mathlib supplies scalar binomial-to-Poisson probability limits. This theorem gives joint weak convergence for finitely many disjoint measurable categories, moving laws and arbitrary diverging sample sizes.
notes: The number of categories is fixed and observations are independent with the same law within each row. Disjointness is required in every row. Rates may be zero; no separate convergence of count moments is asserted.
statement:
Fix a natural number $k$. Let $m_n\in\mathbb N$ tend to infinity, let $P_n$ be probability measures on an arbitrary measurable space $E$, and let $A_{n1},\ldots,A_{nk}$ be measurable and pairwise disjoint within each row. For nonnegative rates $\lambda_i$, assume
$$
m_nP_n(A_{ni})\longrightarrow\lambda_i\qquad(i=1,\ldots,k).
$$
Under $P_n^{\otimes m_n}$, form the count vector $C_{ni}=\sum_{j<m_n}\mathbf1\{X_j\in A_{ni}\}$. Then $C_n$ converges weakly to $\bigotimes_{i=1}^k\operatorname{Poisson}(\lambda_i)$ as a law on $\mathbb N^k$. The formal conclusion is convergence of expectations of every bounded continuous real function on this finite product of discrete count spaces; the product sample space may change with $n$.
summary: Counts in finitely many disjoint moving rare categories converge jointly to independent Poisson laws.
title: Poisson limits for moving rare-category counts
use: A joint law-of-small-numbers interface for shrinking windows and categorical rare events, including triangular arrays with changing distributions and sample sizes. The interval-category corollary supplies local-density rates for windows shrinking around a fixed point.

mathlib_relation: The proof uses Mathlib v4.34.1 variance_sum_pi, variance_const_mul and variance_eq_sub, together with finite uniform-measure integral identities. The theorem expresses ordinary-bootstrap sample-mean variance through this variance algebra.
notes: The empirical variance on the right uses divisor n. The bootstrap variance is the exact average over all resamples; the theorem makes no claim about a variance estimated from finitely many simulated bootstrap replicates. Asymptotic consistency requires additional hypotheses in the companion theorem.

related_declarations.role: bootstrap variance and standard-error consistency under iid finite-second-moment and positive-variance assumptions
finite-resample sum as a product-law integral

statement:
For every natural number $n>0$ and every fixed real sample $x_1,\ldots,x_n$, let $\bar x=n^{-1}\sum_i x_i$. For each resampling map $a:\{1,\ldots,n\}\to\{1,\ldots,n\}$, let $\bar x_a=n^{-1}\sum_i x_{a(i)}$. The definition of the ideal ordinary-bootstrap variance averages $(\bar x_a-\bar x_*)^2$ over all $n^n$ maps with equal weights, where $\bar x_*$ is their average. Then
$$
n\operatorname{Var}_*(\bar x_a)=\frac1n\sum_i x_i^2-\bar x^2.
$$
There is no population law, independence assumption on the supplied sample, or asymptotic hypothesis in this declaration.
summary: The ideal ordinary-bootstrap variance of a fixed sample mean equals its empirical variance divided by sample size.
title: Exact ordinary-bootstrap variance of the sample mean
use: An exact finite-sample identity for checking bootstrap mean implementations and reducing ideal-bootstrap variance consistency to consistency of the empirical second moment. It is valid for every nonempty fixed sample, including a singleton.

mathlib_relation: Mathlib v4.34.1 supplies CDFs, integrals and L2/Vitali tools. This declaration gives a quantile/CDF truncation inequality. The quantile definition and indicator-to-CDF transport identity come from the bundled Causalean library.
notes: Both quantiles must be square integrable. The tail cutoffs include equality. The conclusion is a deterministic inequality for two real laws and does not itself assert a sampling or convergence result.

related_declarations.role: squared error between finite empirical quantiles
mean convergence under uniform square tails

statement:
Let $\mu,\nu$ be Borel probability measures on $\mathbb R$ whose lower generalized-inverse quantiles $Q_\mu,Q_\nu$ belong to $L^2((0,1),du)$. For every real $C\ge0$,
$$
\int_0^1[Q_\mu(u)-Q_\nu(u)]^2\,du
\le4\int x^2\mathbf1\{x^2\ge C^2\}\,d\mu(x)
+4\int x^2\mathbf1\{x^2\ge C^2\}\,d\nu(x)
+2C\int_{-C}^{C}|F_\mu(x)-F_\nu(x)|\,dx.
$$
The unit-level measure in the signature is Lebesgue measure restricted to $(0,1)$; $F_\mu,F_\nu$ are the Mathlib CDFs.
summary: Squared quantile distance is bounded by marginal square tails and an integrated CDF difference on a compact interval.
title: Squared quantile error from tails and CDF distance
use: Separates quantile approximation into tail control and CDF approximation on a bounded interval. It applies to empirical, atomic, mixed and continuous laws, and is useful when a uniform CDF bound is unavailable.

mathlib_relation: Mathlib supplies CDFs and finite probability measures. This result identifies the local ceiling-rank empirical quantile with the lower generalized inverse defined in bundled Causalean code.
notes: Only strictly interior levels are covered by this declaration. It makes no endpoint equality claim and uses the ceiling-rank convention rather than an interpolated sample quantile. This is an interface identity, not an additional statistical limit theorem.
statement:
For every natural number $N>0$, every real sample $y:\{1,\ldots,N\}\to\mathbb R$, and every $u$ with $0<u<1$, let $\widehat\mu_y=N^{-1}\sum_i\delta_{y_i}$. Then
$$
y_{(\lceil Nu\rceil)}=Q_{\widehat\mu_y}(u),
$$
where the left side is the audit’s empirical quantile, using increasing order statistics with multiplicities, and $Q_\mu(u)=\inf\{x:u\le F_\mu(x)\}$ is the Causalean lower generalized inverse of the Mathlib CDF. The equality is pointwise for each such $u$.
summary: For a nonempty finite sample, the ceiling-rank empirical quantile equals the generalized inverse at every interior probability level.
title: Empirical ceiling-rank quantile equals the generalized inverse
use: Makes finite order-statistic formulas interoperable with general quantile transport and coupling theorems. Ties and atoms are allowed, and the almost-everywhere companion supports integrals of arbitrary functions of the quantile.

mathlib_relation: Mathlib v4.34.1 supplies integration and uniform-integrability tools. This finite-population mean quantile-approximation theorem uses the P022 sampling bounds and the bundled Causalean quantile base.
notes: The injection enforces sampling without replacement; no lower bound on the sampling fraction is assumed. Uniform square-tail control is stronger than separate finite second moments in every row. The P022 design type carries auxiliary treatment/control size restrictions even though the sampled block here is any injection.

related_declarations.role: finite mean bound before passage to the limit

statement:
For each $n$, let $d_n$ be a P022 finite design. Its built-in conditions are $N_n\ge4$ and auxiliary arm sizes $a_n,b_n\ge2$ with $a_n+b_n\le N_n$. Let $s_n\ge1$, let $e_n:\{1,\ldots,s_n\}\to\{1,\ldots,N_n\}$ be injective, let $y_n$ be an arbitrary real population array, and suppose $s_n\to\infty$. Assume uniform square-tail control: for every $\varepsilon>0$ there is a real $\beta>1$ such that for every $n$,
$$
\frac1{N_n}\sum_i y_{ni}^2\mathbf1\{y_{ni}^2\ge\beta\}\le\varepsilon.
$$
Let $\pi$ be uniform over all permutations of the $N_n$ labels. Write $\widehat\mu_{n,\pi}$ for the empirical law of $y_{n,\pi(e_n(j))}$ over $j\le s_n$, and $\mu_n$ for the full-population empirical law. Then
$$
E_\pi\left[\int_0^1[Q_{\widehat\mu_{n,\pi}}(u)-Q_{\mu_n}(u)]^2\,du\right]\longrightarrow0.
$$
The expectation is the exact finite average over the row-specific permutation design.
summary: Growing samples without replacement approximate population quantiles in mean squared distance under uniform square-tail control.
title: Mean squared quantile approximation without replacement
use: Provides mean convergence of empirical quantiles to finite-population quantiles for sampling without replacement, without a common probability space for assignments or an assumed limiting population law. The probability-convergence companion follows by a finite-design Markov bound.

group: Finite randomization, inclusion probabilities and variance
mathlib_relation: Mathlib v4.34.1 supplies finite-sum and integral linearity. Exposure-mean unbiasedness here follows from an elementary finite weighted-sum identity.
notes: Probabilities are the exact known design probabilities. The theorem assumes fixed exposure-specific potential outcomes; it does not address estimated propensities, consistency, or loss of reports unless that loss is encoded in the population outcomes. It also includes the empty-unit case through total division.
statement:
Let $\Omega$ be a finite assignment type with strictly positive real weights summing to one, and let $N,K$ be natural numbers. A population supplies an exposure map $D:\Omega\to\{0,\ldots,N-1\}\to\{0,\ldots,K-1\}$ and fixed real potential outcomes $y_i(d)$. Choose a target exposure $d$ and assume $\pi_i(d)=E[\mathbf1\{D_i=d\}]>0$ for every unit $i$. Define
$$
\widehat\mu_{HT}(d)=\frac1N\sum_{i<N}\frac{\mathbf1\{D_i=d\}y_i(d)}{\pi_i(d)},\qquad \mu(d)=\frac1N\sum_{i<N}y_i(d).
$$
Then $E[\widehat\mu_{HT}(d)]=\mu(d)$. The statement has no strict upper bound on $\pi_i(d)$ and no hypothesis $N>0$; when $N=0$, both means are zero under Lean's total division convention.
summary: A Horvitz–Thompson exposure mean is unbiased whenever every target exposure probability is positive.
title: Horvitz–Thompson unbiasedness with positive exposure marginals
use: Provides the basic design-unbiased exposure-mean interface under arbitrary finite assignment and exposure mappings, including interference. Exposure probability one is allowed. The observed_exposure_sum companion connects the masked potential-outcome formula to observed outcomes; recorded_unbiased applies it to fixed recording indicators.

group: Finite randomization, inclusion probabilities and variance
mathlib_relation: Mathlib supplies finite matrix and sum algebra. The binary-treatment Gram inverse, OLS residuals, leverage and HC2 sandwich are defined here, together with the equality to the Neyman variance expression.
notes: Applies to an intercept and a single binary treatment indicator, with at least two observations in each arm. It states neither randomization-expectation conservativeness nor a standard-error identity, and it does not cover covariate-adjusted specifications.

related_declarations.role: Treatment diagonal of the HC2 sandwich

statement:
Let $\iota$ be any finite type, $s\subseteq\iota$ a treatment arm, and $Y:\iota\to\mathbb R$ arbitrary outcomes. Suppose $n_1=\#s\ge2$ and $n_0=\#s^c\ge2$. In OLS of $Y$ on an intercept and $\mathbf1\{i\in s\}$, let $e_i$ be the fitted residual, $h_i$ the leverage, and $x_i=(1,\mathbf1\{i\in s\})^T$. The slope diagonal of the HC2 sandwich
$$
(X^TX)^{-1}\left(\sum_i\frac{e_i^2}{1-h_i}x_ix_i^T\right)(X^TX)^{-1}
$$
equals $s_1^2/n_1+s_0^2/n_0$, where $s_a^2$ is the within-arm sample variance with divisor $n_a-1$. This is an equality for every fixed $s,Y$.
summary: The treatment-slope HC2 variance equals the Neyman variance formula for every assignment with at least two observations per arm.
title: Unadjusted HC2 equals the Neyman variance estimator
use: Connects the matrix HC2 calculation to the familiar design-based variance estimator. It is useful for checking implementations of unadjusted binary-treatment regression on arbitrary finite samples, without a stochastic model for the outcomes.

mathlib_relation: Mathlib v4.34.1 provides scalar iid CLTs, multivariate Gaussian laws, characteristic functions and product measures. This theorem combines these ingredients with local pair and overlap calculations to obtain a vector pair-score CLT and overlap-meat consistency.
notes: Fixed finite dimension, uniformly bounded kernel, pointwise symmetry and coordinatewise centering. The complete unordered-pair set is used, while the meat sums ordered overlapping pairs including equal dyads. Singular covariance is allowed; no inverse-covariance or studentized limit is asserted.

statement:
Let $\mu$ be a probability measure on any measurable type $U$ and $k$ any finite dimension. Let $h:U\times U\to\mathbb R^k$ be measurable and pointwise symmetric, with $\|h(u,v)\|\le B$ for some real $B$ and all $u,v$, and with $\int h_j\,d(\mu\otimes\mu)=0$ for every coordinate $j$. Define $g_j(u)=\int h_j(u,v)\,d\mu(v)$ and $\Gamma_{j\ell}=\int g_j(u)g_\ell(u)\,d\mu(u)$. For each $N$, use the iid row law $P_N=\mu^{\{0,\ldots,N-1\}}$, put $D_N=N(N-1)/2$, and for each unordered two-element dyad $d$ let $H_d=h(U_i,U_j)$ for its two endpoints. Define the ordered overlap meat
$$
M_N=\sum_{d,f:\ d\cap f\ne\varnothing}H_dH_f^T.
$$
Then $NM_N/D_N^2\to4\Gamma$ in probability: for every $\varepsilon>0$, the $P_N$-probability that the norm of the error is at least $\varepsilon$ tends to zero. Also there exists a probability law $G$ on $\mathbb R^k$ with positive-semidefinite covariance $4\Gamma$, whose every real linear contrast is mean-zero Gaussian with the corresponding quadratic-form variance, such that
$$
\frac{\sqrt N}{D_N}\sum_d H_d\ \Rightarrow\ G.
$$
The row statistics are almost everywhere measurable, and the latter convergence uses all bounded continuous real test functions on these changing finite product spaces.
summary: Bounded symmetric vector pair scores have a Gaussian limit and a consistent overlap-based covariance matrix.
title: Bounded vector pair-kernel CLT and overlap-meat consistency
use: Pairs a multivariate pair-average CLT with consistency of the overlap-based covariance matrix. This supports vector dyadic scores and sandwich calculations, allowing singular projection covariance. It adds vector and covariance-estimation conclusions to the scalar second-moment CLT, at the cost of boundedness.

notes: The declaration proves sufficiency of the displayed feasibility inequalities. It does not separately state their necessity or impose any independence between the coordinates.

statement:
For any natural number $K$, numbers $p_i\in[0,1]$ for $i\in\{0,\ldots,K-1\}$, and real $\alpha$ satisfying
$$
0\le\alpha\le1,\qquad \alpha\le p_i\ \text{for every }i,\qquad
1-\sum_i(1-p_i)\le\alpha,
$$
there exist real weights $w(s)$ on all Boolean vectors $s\in\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}^K$ such that
$$
w(s)\ge0,\qquad \sum_s w(s)=1,\qquad
\sum_{s:s_i=\mathrm{true}}w(s)=p_i\ \text{for every }i,\qquad
w(\mathrm{true},\ldots,\mathrm{true})=\alpha.
$$
The quantifier includes $K=0$, where the hypotheses force $\alpha=1$.
summary: Every feasible common success probability is attained by a finite joint distribution with the prescribed Bernoulli marginals.
title: Bernoulli coupling with prescribed all-success mass
use: A small finite coupling construction for attaining intersection-probability bounds, joint-status models and sharp identification arguments. It gives a joint mass function without requiring strictly positive probabilities for every status vector; its splitting argument uses only finite sums and real arithmetic.

group: Dependency-graph quadratic forms and spectral repair
mathlib_relation: Mathlib supplies finite equivalence classes and matrix PSD criteria, including the zero-quadratic-form kernel property. The graph characterization uses local Boolean-graph and PSD definitions and expresses clique quadratic forms as cluster sums of squares.
notes: Singleton cliques and empty graphs are allowed. The formula concerns centered scores and ordered matrix-pair sums; it does not assert stochastic conservativeness.

related_declarations.role: transitivity definition for a union of cliques

statement:
For any natural number $n$ and any simple undirected graph $A$ on $\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$, write $S=I+\operatorname{adj}(A)$. Then $S$ is positive semidefinite if and only if equality-or-adjacency is transitive, that is, $A$ is a disjoint union of cliques. Moreover, for every labeling $C:\{0,\ldots,n-1\}\to\mathbb N$ satisfying
$$
A(i,j)=\mathrm{true}\ \Longleftrightarrow\ i\ne j\ \text{and}\ C_i=C_j,
$$
and every real vector $x$, let $\bar x=n^{-1}\sum_i x_i$ and $e_i=x_i-\bar x$. The declaration also asserts
$$
V_1(A,x)=\frac{\sum_i e_i^2+\sum_{i,j}\operatorname{adj}(A)_{ij}e_ie_j}{n^2}
=\frac{1}{n^2}\sum_{c\in\operatorname{image}(C)}\left(\sum_{i:C_i=c}e_i\right)^2.
$$
There is no positive-size hypothesis; at $n=0$ the source uses Lean's totalized division convention.
summary: Identity plus adjacency is positive semidefinite exactly for unions of cliques and then yields a cluster sum-of-squares formula.
title: Positive semidefinite graph matrices and unions of cliques
use: Characterizes precisely when the identity-plus-adjacency quadratic estimator is PSD before spectral repair, and turns clique dependence into a familiar cluster sum-of-squares formula. A companion theorem constructs suitable cluster labels; the result is purely finite algebra and imposes no stochastic model.

mathlib_relation: Mathlib v4.34.1 supplies Gaussian laws, CDFs and convergence-in-measure infrastructure. This bootstrap-median variance counterexample uses the P001 iid, CDF-limit and conditional-bootstrap-test interfaces.
notes: The selected declaration concerns odd sample sizes and exact ordinary-bootstrap variance, not a finite Monte Carlo estimate of that variance. The population has local density one quarter at median zero; local regularity alone does not control bootstrap second moments.
statement:
Let $\mu$ be any probability measure and let $(X_i)_{i\ge0}$ be measurable iid real variables under $\mu$, with common law
$$
\tfrac12\,\mathrm{Uniform}[-1,1]+\tfrac14\,\mathcal L(2^{1/U^2})+\tfrac14\,\mathcal L(-2^{1/U^2}),\qquad U\sim\mathrm{Uniform}[0,1].
$$
Let $M_n$ be the sample median, and let $M_n^*$ recompute it on an ordinary size-$n$ sample drawn with replacement from the first $n$ observations. Write $V_n^*=\operatorname{Var}^*(M_n^*)$, the exact finite conditional variance over all $n^n$ resampling maps. Along $n=2k+1$, the declaration asserts CDF convergence $\sqrt n M_n\Rightarrow N(0,4)$ and conditional bootstrap weak convergence in probability: for every bounded continuous real $f$,
$$
E^*f\!\left(\sqrt n(M_n^*-M_n)\right)\ \longrightarrow_p\ \int f\,dN(0,4).
$$
It also asserts, for every odd $n\ge5$,
$$
\mu(nV_n^*>5)\ge\frac{3}{16},
$$
and $nV_n^*$ does not converge in probability to $4$ along $n=2k+1$.
summary: A heavy-tailed median has valid sampling and bootstrap weak limits while its scaled bootstrap variance remains inconsistent.
title: Weak bootstrap validity need not give variance consistency
use: Separates weak bootstrap validity from convergence of bootstrap moments using the actual sample median. The population is regular near its median, but remote tails make rare resamples influential for conditional variance. It is a concrete warning when bootstrap standard errors are justified only by a weak limit.

mathlib_relation: Mathlib v4.34.1 provides product laws, finite sums, moments and probability convergence tools. The matching and exact-resampling definitions are local to P001.
notes: The bootstrap conclusion is convergence of its variance expectation to the smaller constant, plus failure of convergence in probability to the sampling constant. It does not claim convergence in probability to the smaller constant.

statement:
On any probability space let $(P_i,A_i,E_i)_{i\ge0}$ be measurable iid observations from `matchingUnitLaw`: $P_i\sim\mathrm{Uniform}[1/4,3/4]$, $A_i\mid P_i\sim\mathrm{Bernoulli}(P_i)$, and $E_i$ is an independent fair sign. For each treated unit match to the untreated unit with nearest $P$; the source fixes a tie choice and assigns a zero contribution when no untreated donor exists. The statistic `causalMatch` is
$$
T_n=-\frac1n\left(\sum_{i:A_i=0}E_i+\sum_{i:A_i=1}E_{j(i)}\right),
$$
with the stated no-donor convention. Let $V_n^*=\operatorname{Var}^*(T_n^*)$ be its exact ordinary-bootstrap variance, recomputing matches on every resample. Then $E_\mu T_n=0$ for every $n>0$,
$$
n\operatorname{Var}_\mu(T_n)\to V,\qquad E_\mu[nV_n^*]\to V_B,\qquad 0<V_B<V,
$$
and $nV_n^*$ does not converge in probability to $V$. The constants are $V=3\log3-1/4$ and
$$
s=1-e^{-1},\quad a=2/s-s/(2-s),\quad b=3/(2s)-(4-s)/(2(2-s)),\quad
V_B=1/2+a/2+b(2\log3-3/2).
$$
summary: An exactly unbiased nearest-neighbor matching estimator has an inconsistent ordinary bootstrap variance with a smaller expectation limit.
title: Nearest-neighbor matching can defeat the ordinary bootstrap variance
use: Shows that bootstrap variance failure for nearest-neighbor matching need not be caused by estimator bias: unbiasedness holds at every positive sample size. The same development has a hot-deck counterpart and extensions to the source’s estimated-score statistic. The result is for a specified continuous-score design, rather than arbitrary matching procedures.

mathlib_relation: Mathlib supplies Cauchy densities, improper integrals, Fubini–Tonelli tools and almost-everywhere integrability of slices through MeasureTheory.Integrable.prod_left_ae. The explicit smooth positive density has an exceptional slice consistent with that almost-everywhere theorem.
notes: The exceptional slice has infinite nonnegative extended integral. This infinite value is not represented by Lean’s totalized real Bochner integral.

statement:
Define, for all real $x,y$,
$$
f(x,y)=\frac{(e^x/(1+e^x))^2}{\pi(1+y^2e^{2x})}.
$$
The declaration asserts jointly that $f$ is infinitely differentiable on $\mathbb R^2$, $f(x,y)>0$ everywhere, $f$ is Lebesgue integrable on $\mathbb R^2$, and $\int_{\mathbb R^2}f=1$. Nevertheless,
$$
\int_{\mathbb R}^{-}\operatorname{ofReal}(f(x,0))\,dx=+\infty,
$$
where this is the nonnegative extended Lebesgue integral. For every real $y\ne0$, the function $x\mapsto f(x,y)$ is Lebesgue integrable.
summary: A smooth strictly positive joint density can have an infinite marginal slice at one point despite finite total mass.
title: A smooth positive density can have an infinite exceptional marginal slice
use: A concrete distinction between pointwise claims about marginal-density formulas and the almost-everywhere conclusions supplied by Fubini and Tonelli. The proof normalizes Cauchy conditional densities using a logistic mixing density; the failure is confined to the exceptional slice at zero.

mathlib_relation: Mathlib v4.34.1 provides finite probability laws, covariance, Gaussian laws and convergence infrastructure. The counterexample uses P018 definitions of OLS, overlap meat and bounded-continuous-test weak limits.
notes: Matrix coordinates in the statement use statistical numbering; Lean’s slope coordinate is 1. The pivot is totalized: Real.sqrt of a negative estimate is zero and division by zero is zero. The claim concerns that specified pivot and an absolute matrix error scale.

failure of the normal pivot limit

statement:
Take iid units $(Z_i,W_i)$ consisting of two independent fair signs, observe all unordered distinct dyads, and set $X_{ij}=(1,1+Z_iZ_j)$ and $Y_{ij}=W_i+W_j$. Let $Q=E[X_{12}X_{12}^{\mathsf T}]$, $\beta=Q^{-1}E[X_{12}Y_{12}]$, $h_{ij}=X_{ij}(Y_{ij}-X_{ij}^{\mathsf T}\beta)$, and $\Gamma=E[g(U)g(U)^{\mathsf T}]$ for $g(u)=E[h(u,U')]$. Let $\widehat V_N$ be the OLS residual sandwich with all ordered pairs of dyads sharing at least one unit in its meat, including identical dyads, and let $D_N=N(N-1)/2$. The declaration asserts the source's standing conditions: a probability unit law, measurable symmetric bounded dyad data, an intercept and nonsingular $Q$. It also asserts `Proposition1Extra`: uniformly bounded fitted residuals at every size; nonzero entries of $Q$ and of $E[X_{12}X_{13}^{\mathsf T}]$; and eventually in $N$, nonzero expected fitted-residual squares and nonzero expected fitted-residual products for every pair of distinct overlapping dyads.

Its population identities are
$$
Q=\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\1&2\end{pmatrix},\qquad \beta=0,\qquad
\Gamma=\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\1&1\end{pmatrix},\qquad
4Q^{-1}\Gamma Q^{-1}=\operatorname{diag}(4,0).
$$
For every $N\ge3$, the source's unconditional covariance target is
$$
V_N=\frac{N}{D_N^2}Q^{-1}\operatorname{Var}\!\left(\sum_{i<j}h_{ij}\right)Q^{-1}
=\begin{pmatrix}4N/(N-1)&-4/(N-1)\\-4/(N-1)&4/(N-1)\end{pmatrix}.
$$
Finally,
$$
P((\widehat V_N)_{22}<0)\to1-e^{-1/2},\qquad
N\widehat V_N\longrightarrow_p\operatorname{diag}(4,0),
$$
while $(\widehat\beta_{N,2}-\beta_2)/\sqrt{(\widehat V_N)_{22}}$ does not converge weakly to $N(0,1)$ under the source's bounded-continuous-test definition.
summary: A bounded dyadic model has an absolutely consistent sandwich matrix, a negative estimated slope variance with positive limiting probability, and a totalized slope pivot without a standard normal limit.
title: Absolute sandwich consistency does not validate a degenerate contrast
use: Demonstrates that absolute consistency of a covariance estimator does not justify studentization of a contrast whose limiting variance is zero, even with bounded iid unit characteristics and the source’s additional moment conditions. The same development supplies an explicit eight-unit negative-variance certificate.

mathlib_relation: Mathlib v4.34.1 provides Pareto distributions, matrix inversion, finite products and convergence-in-measure tools. The dyadic inverse-Gram infinite-moment witness uses these ingredients within the P018 kernel model.
notes: The divergence is a nonnegative extended expectation of the inverse Euclidean operator norm, not a finite real expectation. Outcomes are identically zero, so this does not exhibit infinite moments of fitted OLS coefficients. Probability convergence uses varying finite product sample spaces.

related_declarations.role: bounded dyadic design with zero outcomes

statement:
Let iid real unit characteristics $T_i$ have density $t^{-2}\mathbf1\{t\ge1\}$. On all unordered distinct dyads take $X_{ij}=(1,e^{-T_i}+e^{-T_j})$ and $Y_{ij}=0$. Put $D_N=N(N-1)/2$, $Q=E[X_{12}X_{12}^{\mathsf T}]$, and $Q_N=D_N^{-1}\sum_{i<j}X_{ij}X_{ij}^{\mathsf T}$. The declaration asserts `Standing`: the unit law is a probability, the dyad functions are measurable and symmetric, are bounded almost surely under the two-unit product law, an intercept is present, and $Q$ is nonsingular. It also asserts `SampleRank`: some deterministic $N_0$ gives almost-sure nonsingularity of the sample Gram matrix for each $N\ge N_0$. Under the finite iid product law at size $N$,
$$
Q_N^{-1}-Q^{-1}\longrightarrow_p0.
$$
For every integer $N\ge3$ and integer $m\ge1$ it additionally gives the quantitative lower bound
$$
\operatorname{ofReal}\!\left(\frac{e^{2m}}{4m^N}\right)
\le\int^{-}\operatorname{ofReal}\!\left(\|Q_N^{-1}\|_{\mathrm{op}}\right)\,dP_N,
$$
and for every integer $N\ge3$ this nonnegative extended integral equals $+\infty$. The displayed operator norm is the Euclidean induced norm.
summary: A bounded full-rank dyadic design has a probability limit for its inverse Gram matrix but infinite inverse-norm expectation at every relevant size.
title: Inverse continuity does not imply inverse-moment control
use: A concrete obstruction to replacing probability convergence of inverse sample matrices with inverse-moment bounds. It isolates a design-matrix problem in bounded regressors and shows exactly how a small-probability nearly singular design can dominate expectation.

mathlib_relation: Mathlib supplies rank-one operators, their norm formula, finite-sum variance and convergence tools. The counterexample combines these ingredients with the local centering and variance-form definitions.
notes: This is a fixed iid-sign witness with a matrix selected from the same data. It does not refute the deterministic-matrix theorem. The limits use size n equal to k plus one and its corresponding finite sample law.
statement:
For every integer $n>0$ and every sign vector $x\in\{-1,1\}^n$, define $\bar x=n^{-1}\sum_i x_i$, $M(x)=xx^{\mathsf T}/n$, and
$$
\operatorname{varianceForm}(M,x)=\frac{(x-\bar x\mathbf1)^{\mathsf T}M(x-\bar x\mathbf1)}{n^2}.
$$
The declaration asserts the exact identities
$$
\|M(x)\|_{\mathrm{op}}=1,\qquad\operatorname{tr}M(x)=1,\qquad
n\,\operatorname{varianceForm}(M(x),x)=(1-\bar x^2)^2.
$$
For $n=k+1$ and a vector $X$ of $n$ independent fair signs, under its size-specific joint law it further asserts
$$
n\,\operatorname{varianceForm}(M(X),X)-1\longrightarrow_p0,\qquad
\frac{\operatorname{tr}(M(X)-I_n)}{n}\longrightarrow_p-1.
$$
summary: A rank-one matrix selected from iid signs breaks the deterministic quadratic expansion despite having bounded operator norm.
title: A deterministic-matrix expansion can fail after data selection
use: An exact counterexample to extending a deterministic-matrix quadratic expansion to a matrix selected from the same observations using only an operator-norm bound. The finite identity makes the mismatch visible before taking limits; the probability limit follows from the iid-sign sample mean tending to zero.

statement:
The declaration has no hypotheses and establishes the concrete proposition `EqualCompletionFailure`. On the 32 configurations $(u,r_0,r_1,x,t)\in\{0,1\}^5$, give each configuration weight
$$
\frac18\,p_0(u)^{r_0}(1-p_0(u))^{1-r_0}p_1(u)^{r_1}(1-p_1(u))^{1-r_1},
$$
where $p_b(u)=37/50$ if $b=u$ and $13/50$ otherwise. Set $T=t$, $Y(0)=Y(1)=u$, $R(b)=r_b$, and $X=x$, with realized completion $R=R(T)$. The conclusion is that $T$ is independent of the entire potential-outcome, potential-completion and covariate bundle; $P(R=1\mid T=b)=1/2$ for both arms; $R(0)$ is independent of neither $u$ nor $(u,u,x)$; and the population treatment effect is zero. For respondent design vector $z=(1,T,X)$, the vector $\beta=(13/50,12/25,0)$ solves $E[zz^\top\mid R=1]\beta=E[zY\mid R=1]$, while its treatment coefficient $12/25$ differs from the zero population effect.
summary: Equal response rates across randomized treatment arms can coexist with a biased complete-case regression coefficient.
title: Equal completion rates do not identify a complete-case treatment effect
use: A finite diagnostic example for attrition assumptions: equal arm response rates do not supply independence of potential response from outcomes and covariates. It concerns complete-case population normal equations with one binary covariate.

notes: The example concerns a nonlinear XOR prediction under this three-unit assignment design. It does not assert failure under independence from the whole fitting vector.
